pr_title: e2e flake CheckDaemonStatus assert on async value
pr_body:
The util for checking on daemonstatus was checking once if the Status of the daemonset was reporting that all the desired Pods are scheduled and ready.

However, the pattern used in the e2e test for this function was not taking into consideration that the controller needs to propagate the Pod status to the DeamonSet status, and was asserting on the condition only once after waiting for all the Pods to be ready.

In order to avoid more churn code, change the CheckDaemonStatus signature to the wait.Condition type and use it in a async poll loop on the tests.

/kind flake
```release-note
NONE
```

Fixes: #128049

/assign @soltysh @pohly 
/sig apps

review_comments:
My usual objection against using `wait.PollUntilContextTimeout` in E2E tests applies here: if this fails, there is not information in the failure message about the actual state, just the usual useless  "timed out" error.

There's also no progress information while it waits.

But I don't care enough about this (anymore) to argue about it.
I missed that you changed the prototype of a function in the e2e/framework so that it works well with `wait.PollUntilContextTimeout`. The revised function now also pollutes the test output with a log message on each retry.

I care less about tests (this code here), but I care about the e2e/framework enough that I'll submit a followup-PR... stay tuned.

> In order to avoid more churn code, change the CheckDaemonStatus signature to the wait.Condition type and use it in a async poll loop on the tests.

Even less code churn would have been to do the polling inside the helper function. Then tests wouldn't have to be modified at all.
The reason why I noticed and why I care is because I am using `CheckDaemonStatus` in one of my branches for DRA where I am testing with a daemon set and that broke when rebasing.

=> https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128079
Thanks
